key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the aluminum alloy sheet
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the aluminum alloy coil in China

The Chinese aluminum coil is also classified in heading 7606. For 7606, 19 CFR 102.20 requires a change from any other heading; thus, the Canadian slitting, painting, cutting, and notching fail the 102.11(a)(3) tariff shift (similar to N316637 and N316780). key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the solar cells
decisive_step: manufacture of the crystalline silicon solar cells in China
flip: Manufacture the solar cells in Mexico so that all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3).
reasoning: Following H266527, solar panels without elements allowing power supply directly to a load are classified in heading 8541 (8541.43). Under 19 CFR 102.20(o), heading 8541 requires a change to 8541.10-8541.90 from any other subheading, or from within that group whether or not also from any other subheading provided a change from a wafer to a cell occurs. Assembling imported foreign solar cells (ordinarily from China) into panels in Mexico fails the tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3). Under 102.11(b)(1), the solar cells impart the essential character.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the US cereal flakes
decisive_step: production of the cereal flakes in the United States, the only foreign material failing the tariff shift to heading 1904
flip: Source the cereal flakes from Canada, allowing all foreign ingredients to satisfy the tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and conferring Canadian origin.
reasoning: The cereal is classified in heading 1904 (prepared foods obtained from cereals). The 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for heading 1904 requires a change from any other heading. All foreign ingredients mixed in Canada shift to 1904 except the US-origin cereal flakes (already classified in heading 1904). Under 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1) and 102.18(b)(1)(iii), because the US cereal flakes are the single foreign material that fails the tariff shift, they impart the essential character, making the origin the United States (see H312440).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 8473
decisive_step: Soldering, stacking, and oven-brazing the Chinese components into finished thermal modules in Mexico

reasoning: The finished Thermal Modules are classified under subheading 8473.30.5100. For heading 8473, 19 CFR 102.20(o) requires a change to heading 8473 from any other heading. Through soldering, stacking, and high-temperature oven assembly in Mexico (which exceeds simple assembly under 102.17), every foreign material undergoes the required tariff shift, conferring Mexican origin under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 2208.50
decisive_step: Macerating neutral grain alcohol with juniper and botanicals, redistilling, and diluting with water into gin in Canada
flip: If the juniper maceration and redistillation occurred in the Netherlands using Dutch neutral grain alcohol, and only water dilution and bottling occurred in Canada (non-qualifying under 102.17), the origin would be the Netherlands.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8421.29

decisive_step: Fabrication and cutting/drilling of the MDF/acrylic panels and packaging of the disassembled wine rack kit in Canada

key_factors: (d)(3) last country in which the good underwent production

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 3824.99

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7326
decisive_step: Slitting, stamping, perforating, and assembling the stainless steel strip and screw into complete hose clamps in Canada

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8483.40
decisive_step: Machining the rings, cutting the gear teeth, and assembling the slew bearings in Mexico
flip: If the gear teeth were already cut onto the rings in China prior to importation into Mexico, giving the rings the essential character of the finished gear under GRI 2(a), origin would remain China.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 3206.11

reasoning: The finished intake and exhaust engine valves are classified in heading 8409. flip: If a foreign ingredient classified in subheading 2106.90 (such as the natural flavoring, if foreign and classified in 2106.90) failed the tariff shift, analysis would move to 102.11(b), conferring the origin of the single non-shifting material or the material imparting essential character (cane sugar).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8708.99
decisive_step: Pressing the Taiwanese oil seal onto the Indian bearing cone in Mexico to create the automotive hub subassembly
flip: If the attached oil seal did not impart significant non-friction-reducing capabilities and the good remained classified in heading 8482, the Indian bearing cone would fail the tariff shift and confer Indian origin under 102.11(b).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8414.30

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the Japanese TPV / polymer inputs

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 2106.90

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 9401.39

key_factors: (a)(1) wholly obtained or produced in a single country
decisive_step: Collection of the horse semen from stallions in Canada

reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(1), the country of origin of a good is the single country in which the good is wholly obtained or produced. Because the Standardbred horse semen (classified in heading 0511) is collected from live stallions in Canada, it is wholly obtained or produced in Canada.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the sodium bentonite clay

The U.S.-origin raw bentonite clay is also classified in heading 2508 and fails the tariff shift in Canada. Under 102.11(b)(1) and 102.18(b), the single non-shifting material—U.S. bentonite clay—confers U.S. origin.

key_factors: (b)(1) essential character of the bulk Parmesan cheese

Under 102.11(b)(1), the single foreign material that fails the shift and imparts the essential character is the U.S. cheese, making the origin United States.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8714.92
decisive_step: Cutting, laminating, molding, curing, and drilling the carbon fiber sheets into finished bicycle rims in Canada
flip: If the rims were imported into Canada already formed as unfinished rims of subheading 8714.92 and only underwent minor finishing or drilling in Canada, the tariff shift would fail and origin would remain with the country of the unformed rim.
reasoning: Bicycle rims are classified in subheading 8714.92, HTSUS.
